_what_it_measures: whether the chain from funding source to piece of work resolves, through WHICH carrier, how much resolution survives each hop, and whether anyone can observe the hop change

grammars._why_it_matters: the fund code is the root identifier of the whole chain — project id and WBS root are both copies of it
the only live organisational dimension in the FM ledger; its code is a 3-letter org acronym
POSID = <fund code>.<level2>.<level3>... — the 4-level spine is encoded as dot depth, not as a parent key
PSPID is expected to BE the fund code — project-as-fund, a string identity rather than a foreign key

hops.semantic: which funding source pays for this piece of work
hops.designed_carrier: FMMEASURE / Funded Program derivation via FMDERIVE
hops.expected: SUBSTITUTED — the designed carrier is unused and the grammar carries it instead
hops.why: resolves at 99.5% — but through STRING PREFIX of POSID, not through the designed FMMEASURE / Funded Program derivation via FMDERIVE. It works and it is invisible to anyone reading the data model.

hops.semantic: the PS project scaffold and the fund it mirrors
hops.designed_carrier: none — Fund and Project are meant to be independent dimensions
hops.expected: SUBSTITUTED — an inversion the 2017 design explicitly forbade, still load-bearing
hops.why: resolves at 98.8% — but through STRING IDENTITY (PSPID = FINCODE), not through the designed none — Fund and Project are meant to be independent dimensions. It works and it is invisible to anyone reading the data model.

hops.semantic: the WBS element and its project definition
hops.designed_carrier: PRPS.PSPHI -> PROJ.PSPNR (the real SAP foreign key)
hops.actual_carrier: same, plus the string root agrees
hops.why: resolves at 99.8% — but through same, plus the string root agrees, not through the designed PRPS.PSPHI -> PROJ.PSPNR (the real SAP foreign key). It works and it is invisible to anyone reading the data model.

hops.semantic: which C/5 programmatic output this fund serves
hops.expected: UNEVEN — a custom carrier is expected to serve some fund families and not others, with no declared rule for which
hops.why: 20.8% overall, but that average is meaningless: coverage runs from 0.0% to 96.4% across identifier families, including DDDDDDDD, ADADDAAADD with no coverage at all. Some populations are fully carried and others not at all, and nothing declares which — so the rule for who gets a link is undocumented.

hops.semantic: the planning/sector line the fund belongs to
hops.expected: UNEVEN — a custom carrier is expected to serve some fund families and not others, with no declared rule for which
hops.why: the carrier exists and serves only 9.4% of the population — real for those rows, absent for the rest

hops.semantic: the FM actual line and its funding source
the FM actual line and the piece of work it funded
hops.expected: BROKEN — this is the hop the whole model needs and does not have
hops.why: the left key resolves to nothing in any row — the carrier this hop depends on is declared and never populated the mechanism in use (CLASSIC_FM_DERIVATION) cannot produce it, and the mechanism that can (DERIVATION_TOOL_FMDERIVE) was never configured. So the empty column is architectural, not neglect — and adopting Funded Program means standing up a second derivation mechanism and migrating onto it, not configuring a field.

root_cause.and_explains: why the identifier convention exists at all: the grammar is not a shortcut around a working feature, it is the only carrier available under this architecture

hops.semantic: the FM actual line and the availability bucket it consumes
hops.designed_carrier: Fund x Fund Center x commitment item
hops.actual_carrier: same, but the commitment-item leg is collapsed to a grouped bucket
hops.expected: COLLAPSED — many cost categories share one availability pool

resolution._reading: at 63.7% of addresses, 3.99 distinct FIPEX values on average arrive at a SINGLE RCMMTITEM — every cost category there draws on one shared pool

hops.why: 92.6% resolves, and then the detail is destroyed: at 63.7% of addresses several distinct FIPEX arrive at a SINGLE RCMMTITEM. Control still happens on the pooled bucket; attribution to a cost category does not survive it.

consistency_checks.fact: the hierarchy level of a WBS element
consistency_checks.why: the identifier and the structure agree at 99.3% — the convention is load-bearing AND consistent, so reading the level off the code is safe for all but 411 rows
consistency_checks._the_exceptions_are_the_point: every disagreeing row is a node whose identifier claims a position the tree does not give it. Everyone reads the code, so for these everyone is wrong.

memories.subject: cdhdr
memories.fact: the change-document header extract is a FILTERED SUBSET. It carries 57 object classes; cdhdr_history carries 72. Missing from cdhdr: PBC, SETS, SUSR_PROF and every custom Y* class.
memories.implication: NEVER answer 'who changed this' from cdhdr alone. Read cdhdr_history too and reconcile. An object absent from cdhdr has not necessarily stopped changing — it may simply not be in this extract.

memories.subject: cdhdr_history
memories.fact: the fuller change log: 72 object classes, 2024-01-01 to 2026-06-20, and the ONLY store carrying PBC, SETS (hierarchy maintenance), SUSR_PROF (authorisation profiles) and the custom Y* change-document objects.
memories.implication: this is the default change instrument, not the fallback. Hierarchy and authorisation questions can ONLY be answered here.

memories.subject: FMFINCODE
memories.fact: the fund-master change-document class carries ZERO records in either change log, while the fund master holds 67,526 funds
memories.implication: who creates and changes funds cannot be answered from the change log at all. Fall back to A8 attribution against the execution log — it is the only instrument left for the most heavily populated master in the model.
